Oliver Bullough: Oliver Bullough is an award-winning journalist and author from the UK, who specialises in writing about financial crime and money laundering. His most recent books are Everybody Loves Our Dollars, Butler to the World, and Moneyland. His journalism appears in the Guardian, the Economist, the New York Times, the Financial Times and elsewhere.
Olivia Allison: Associate Fellow, Royal United Services Institute and Founder, SECTA Research
Omar Cuevas: Omar Cuevas Sánchez, LL.M., is a corporate legal strategist with a Master of Laws and postgraduate studies in sustainability from Stanford University, backed by over 19 years of international experience in governance, compliance, and the defense of cultural heritage. He has held executive leadership positions as General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer for major multinationals, including Aeromexico, Delta Air Lines and British American Tobacco, and serves as a strategic advisor to executives of Top 10 companies on the London Stock Exchange (LSE).
Paola Esmeralda Rodríguez Adames: Acting Director of Demographic, Social, and Environmental Statistics. Office of Demographic, Social, and Environmental Statistics, Dominican Republic.
Paola Medellin Cervantes: Paola is partner at Medellín & Villalobos and Audit Committee Coordinator for the World Compliance Association Mexico, she is a graduate of Escuela Libre de Derecho and holds a Master’s degree in Regulatory Compliance from the University of Castilla-La Mancha, Spain, as well as postgraduate studies in Constitutional Law and the Adversarial Criminal Justice System from UNAM. With more than 15 years of experience in white-collar criminal litigation, compliance, and anti-money laundering, she previously served at Mexico’s Federal Tax Prosecutor’s Office. She is certified by Mexico’s National Banking and Securities Commission (CNBV) in anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, and holds certifications as a Senior Compliance Officer and Compliance Expert Witness for Spain. She is also training as an auditor with AENOR Mexico for ISO 37001:2016 certification. In academia, she teaches Money Laundering and Criminal Compliance in the postgraduate Criminal Law program at Escuela Libre de Derecho, where she also coordinates the Compliance Diploma Program, and previously served on the Board of Directors of the World Compliance Association, Mexico Chapter.
Parnneh T. Mallobe: Parnneh T. Mallobe is an assertive, dynamic professional with over 10 years of experience seamlessly weaving together anti-corruption advocacy, development communication, youth empowerment, and journalism. Recognized for her exceptional dedication to community service, Parnneh is the recipient of an international service award from the Office of the First Lady of the Republic of Liberia. Operating on both global and national stages, she serves as a member of the Integrity Youth Advisory Board for the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) under its Global Resource for Anti-Corruption, Education, and Youth Empowerment (GRACE). Her high-level international advocacy is marked by a landmark 2023 presentation to States Parties at the Conference of the States Parties on youth involvement in fighting corruption in Africa, drawing insights from consultations with over 500 young Africans, and co-facilitating regional dialogues that shaped official conference recommendations. Adding to her national leadership, she is a proud alumna and ambassador of the Governance and Anti-Corruption Fellowship, an intensive initiative by the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission and NAYMOTE-Liberia. Currently serving as the Communications Officer at Accountability Lab Liberia, Parnneh drives strategic transparency initiatives and community-driven campaigns that foster integrity and civic engagement, scaling governance programs that reach hundreds of communities and thousands of citizens. Her diverse career is firmly rooted in five impactful years in mainstream media, where she specialized in reporting on critical public-interest issues, including gender equality, youth affairs, the extractive industry, judicial proceedings, corruption cases, and war crimes survivor stories. Beyond her institutional and anti-corruption work, Parnneh is the passionate founder of Pama Co. and the Live Authentically Movement, a social enterprise championing body positivity, self-love, confidence, and holistic wellness for young people through mentorship and public talks. She is also an alumna of the Young Political Leadership School Africa (YPLSA) and the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI RLC).
Paul Radu:
Paul Radu is Co-Founder and Head of Innovation at OCCRP. He founded the organization in 2007 with Drew Sullivan. He leads OCCRP’s major investigative projects, scopes regional expansion, and develops new strategies and technology to expose organized crime and corruption across borders.

Paul initiated and led the award-winning Russian, Azerbaijani, and Troika Laundromat investigations, and coined the term “laundromat” to define large scale, all-purpose financial fraud vehicles that are used to launder billions of dollars. He is a co-creator of Investigative Dashboard — a research desk that sifts through datasets to help journalists trace people, companies, and assets — and the Visual Investigative Scenarios software, a tool that lets reporters sketch out the people, institutions, and connections in criminal networks so people can easily follow complex investigations. He is also a co-founder of RISE Project, a platform for investigative reporters in Romania.

Paul is an Ashoka Global Fellow and has held a number of other fellowships, including the Milena Jesenska Press Fellowship, the Rosalyn Carter Fellowship for Mental Health Journalism, the Knight International Journalism Fellowship with the International Center for Journalists as well as a 2009-2010 Stanford Knight Journalism Fellowship. He is a board member for the Global Investigative Journalism Network, a member of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, a member of the jury for the global Sigma Data Journalism Awards, and a member of the Allard Prize advisory board.

Paul is a winner of the Daniel Pearl Award, the Global Shining Light Award, the European Press Prize, and the Skoll Award for Social Entrepreneurship, and was part of the Panama Papers team that won the 2017 Pulitzer Prize in Journalism. He has also authored or contributed to handbooks and digital guides such as “Against Corruption: a collection of essays,” “The Data Journalism Handbook,” and “Follow the Money — A Digital Guide to Tracking Corruption.”
President Bernardo Arévalo:
Member of the Congress of the Republic of Guatemala (2020-2024) and Secretary General of the Semilla Movement (2022-2025).

Without prior involvement in partisan politics, the political crisis in Guatemala propelled him to participate in the founding of the Semilla Movement.

Ph.D. in Philosophy from Utrecht University (Netherlands) and Bachelor of Sociology from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (Israel).

Until December 2019, he served as Senior Advisor for Peace Consolidation in the International Advisory Team of Interpeace (IPAT).

He has led several initiatives and programs for the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and Interpeace, seeking the transformation of the state security apparatus.

He was Deputy Director-General for Research and Development at Interpeace between 2011 and 2013.

Between 2005 and 2011, he was Director of the Joint Program Unit of the United Nations and Interpeace with UNOPS, supporting research and dialogue strategies for peace in Israel, Palestine, Cyprus, and Liberia, among others.

He served as Director and Head of the Interpeace Regional Office for Latin America between 1999 and 2005.

Between 1996 and 1998, he participated in post-conflict consensus management following the signing of the Peace Accords in Guatemala.

He served in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Guatemala for over 12 years, holding various positions, including Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and Ambassador to Spain.

He is the author of several books and articles published in Guatemala and abroad. He is a member of the International Commission for Inclusive Peace, a global initiative that seeks to redefine peacebuilding strategies worldwide.
President Luis Abinader:
He was elected vice president of the Dominican Revolutionary Party at the National Convention in 2005 and was the party’s candidate for Vice President of the Republic in the 2012 presidential elections.

Presidential candidate at the PRM Convention held on April 26, 2015, elected with over 70% of the vote, a victory recognized from the first ballot by the other candidates. He immediately received the support of former President Hipólito Mejía, his main competitor in the convention, and the rest of the PRM leadership.

On July 5, 2020, he won the Presidency of the Dominican Republic with the support of 52.52% of the votes.

This marks the beginning of a new phase in which the President of the Dominican Republic, Luis Abinader, has committed to carrying out a series of profound changes to restore the country’s institutions and enable it to serve the people.
Preston Whitt: Preston is a Senior Programme Officer with WWF US.
Princess Chifiero: Ms. Chifiero is an international development professional with over ten years of experience working with the UN, government institutions and non-governmental organizations. She specializes in good governance, youth empowerment, and anti-corruption, with a proven track record of designing and managing complex technical assistance initiatives. At UNODC Nigeria and UNODC Headquarters in Vienna, she has led more than eight high-impact projects covering business integrity, corruption research (including gender and corruption), corruption risk assessments, youth and anticorruption, and policy and institutional reforms for anti-corruption agencies at both national and subnational levels in Nigeria.
Pushpan Murugiah: Anti-Corruption, Public Accountability & Governance Reform Advisor (Malaysia), Southeast Asian Anti-Corruption Network of CSOs (SEA-CAN)
Rajiv Lall:
Rajiv Lall is a distinguished leader in global finance with over three decades of experience spanning banking, infrastructure finance, private equity, and capital markets. He is best known for his transformative role as Managing Director and CEO of Infrastructure Development Finance Company (IDFC), which he joined in 2005. Under his leadership, IDFC grew into India’s largest infrastructure finance company and in 2015, he founded and launched IDFC Bank, further strengthening his legacy in building institutions that bridge finance and development.

Mr. Lall currently serves as Chairman of CoST – the Infrastructure Transparency Initiative – a global not-for-profit working with countries to improve lives by enhancing transparency, accountability, and value for money in public infrastructure. Through this role, he champions reforms that strengthen investor confidence and improve infrastructure outcomes worldwide.

Earlier in his career, Mr. Lall held senior positions at leading global financial institutions, including Warburg Pincus in New York, Morgan Stanley in Hong Kong, the World Bank in Washington, DC, and the Asian Development Bank in Manila. He has also advised at the highest levels of public policy, serving on multiple committees of the Government of India and the Reserve Bank of India, and representing India at the G20 Working Group on Infrastructure.

He is also a Distinguished Fellow at Artha Global and a Professional Research Fellow at Singapore Management University.
Rajiv S. Joshi:
Prof. Rajiv S. Joshi is an economist, community organizer and entrepreneurial leader working at the intersection of environmental, social and economic justice. Originating from Kenya and India, Rajiv was born in Scotland, where he was nationally elected to represent young people. He has directed the world’s largest Global South-led alliance to end poverty and is a steward to climate action initiatives around the world. He is a co-architect of the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda and Lead Author of the Decisive Decade Inquiry into the Future of Climate Action, commissioned by ex-UN Climate Chief, Christiana Figueres, global climate philanthropy and the Mission 2020 Campaign. He has supported global campaigns and initiatives to phase out fossil fuel , transform transform food systems, end illicit flows of capital, mobilize climate finance, advance the economics of wellbeing and halt biodiversity loss. He is a leading voice in exploring how philanthropy, and other actors, can use catalytic collaboration and high-risk capital to drive systemic change in the face of climate change and other converging crises.

Rajiv served as Associate Dean for Climate Action at the Columbia Climate School, driving its launch with President Obama at COP26 and overseeing programs, including the development of a Global Policy Impact Lab with California Clean Air Regulator Mary Nicholls while advising the Center for Global Energy Policy. As an adjunct Professor at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) he has developed the University’s first class in Climate Technology and Regenerative Entrepreneurship, and is also Co-Chair of the Earth Network on the Social Climate, exploring the intersection of climate impacts, mental health and psychological resilience.

Rajiv is currently Founder & CEO of Bridging Ventures, an agency driving radical collaboration, through content, partnerships and coalitions, to address systemic challenges across generations, sectors and geographies. He has advised some of the worlds leading brands, incubated global programs and curated campaigns designed to drive changes in policy, practice and public opinion. Rajiv was appointed as an Executive-in-Residence at Oxford University’s Saïd Business School and is an advisor to global leaders, grassroots NGOs, Governments, philanthropy and business. He was appointed as a Commissioner on Scotland’s Just Transition Commission alongside current IPCC Chair Jim Skea.

Rajiv served as the first Managing Director of The B Team, a not-for-profit initiative Co-Founded by Sir Richard Branson & Jochen Zeitz, together with Paul Polman, Mary Robinson, Ratan Tata and a growing group of the world’s leading CEOs, Union leaders and former Heads of State. In this role he worked with a range of leading companies including Nike, IKEA, Apple, SalesForce, Mastercard as well as social movements and NGOs including Extinction Rebellion, 350.org, Avaaz, WWF, GCAP, Transparency International, Action Aid, Business & Human Rights Resource Center, Global Witness and Extinction Rebellion, on climate change, human rights, governance and corporate accountability. While helping to build the global B-Corp movement.

Rajiv drove the Global Call to Action Against Poverty serving as Executive Director of the campaign and social movement, which was launched by Nelson Mandela and President Lula in 2005 together with Co- Chairs Kumi Naidoo, Sylvia Borren & Amitabh Behar. He served six years on the Council of Trustees of Oxfam GB and as a member of the Board of CIVICUS, the world alliance for citizen participation, based in Johannesburg where he was also on the Executive Committee. Rajiv was elected twice to represent young people in Scotland as Chair of the Scottish Youth Parliament and was a Senior Consultant with CapGemini. He holds a BA with a First Class Honors in Economics from the Strathclyde Business School in Glasgow and an MPA in International Finance and Economic Policy from the School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) at Columbia University in New York.

Rodrigo Chagas: Professor - Forum Brasileiro de Seguranca Publica and Universidade Federal de Roraima
Sandra Ximena Martinez Rosas: Sandra is a political scientist from the University of the Andes with a Master's degree in Political Science from the same university and a Specialist degree in Democracy and Electoral Systems from Sergio Arboleda University. At Transparency for Colombia, she has led initiatives to combat corruption and promote transparency and accountability in the political and electoral process, with an emphasis on campaign finance. She is an expert in methodologies and practices based on deliberative democracy to promote citizen participation, dialogue with authorities, and influence on public policy development.
Serena Ibrahim:
Serena Ibrahim began her journey as a youth anti-corruption activist, driven by a passion for integrity, justice, and civic engagement. She is the Founder and Executive Director of Youth Against Corruption (YAC), an award-winning youth-led organization that leverages social innovation and entrepreneurship to strengthen governance and combat corruption.

Serena serves as a Board Member of Integrity Initiatives International and an Advisory Board Member of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) GRACE Initiative.

A frequent keynote speaker, Serena has contributed to major international forums and policy dialogues, including the United Nations General Assembly Special Session Against Corruption (UNGASS), UNCAC-related events, OECD forums, and International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) platforms. Through her work, she advocates for greater accountability, ethical leadership, and meaningful youth participation in shaping governance systems.

Beyond her anti-corruption work, Serena is a management consultant and strategic advisor to public sector entities across the GCC region, with expertise in sustainability, smart cities, digital economy, and public sector transformation. She has led and supported large-scale national initiatives, advising governments on institutional transformation, economic competitiveness, and future-ready strategies that drive sustainable and inclusive growth.

Serena holds a Master’s degree in Architecture and an International Joint Master’s Degree in Sustainable Territorial Development from leading European universities. She is currently pursuing an Executive MBA.

At the heart of Serena’s work is the belief that no young person should lose faith in humanity because of corruption, injustice, or failed institutions. She is committed to building a future where integrity, justice, and accountability are the norm, and where young people are empowered to lead positive change in their communities and beyond.
Shawn Teixeira:
Shawn has over 35 years experience at Siemens in various Business Administration, Financial Management, Internal Audit and Compliance leadership roles in both South Africa and Germany. Since 2010 Shawn has focused on Ethics and Governance as Compliance Officer responsible for Africa, Head of Compliance Investigations in Munich, and Head of the Siemens Integrity Initiative in Siemens AG, Legal, Compliance and Intellectual Property in Munich.

Shawn has actively promoted and engaged in Collective Action through the Siemens Integrity Initiative for over 16 years. Established in 2009, the Siemens Integrity Initiative supports organizations and projects that fight corruption and fraud through Collective Action, Education and Training.
Sope Williams: Professor of Public Procurement Law and Deputy Director, African Procurement Law Unit, StellenboschUniversity; co-editor, Routledge Handbook of Gender and Corruption (2025)
Stina Ehrensvärd: With a background in industrial product design, Stina is the founder of Yubico and SIROS Foundation. Co-inventor of the YubiKey strong authentication key, and a leading driver behind FIDO/Passkeys open authentication standards, she has received numerous international awards, and is an accomplished speaker on internet identity, cyber security, and entrepreneurship.
Suzanne Hayden: Suzanne Hayden is an international attorney who served for 20 years as aFederal Prosecutor for the US Department of Justice and with the United Nations Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia. She has advised governments throughout the world on corruption, organized crime, moneylaundering and asset recovery and related legislation and conducted training for prosecutors, judges, police and private sector throughout the world. She has been a US legal advisor in Russia, Hungary and Turkey for anti-money laundering and anti-corruption. In addition to her work as a prosecutor and litigator, Suzanne was an advisor to the Dean of the International Anticorruption Academy in Austria, and a Special Advisor to the Director of the National Counterproliferation Center, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence for the United States. For the past 10 years, Suzanne has worked with civil societies investigating and building prosecutable cases involving wildlife trafficking and environmental crime. She is currently a senior advisor for The Sentry.
Tawakkol Karman:
Tawakkol Karman is a Yemeni human rights defender, journalist, and Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. She is the first Arab woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize, for her nonviolent struggle for democracy, freedom of expression, and women’s rights.

Known as the “Mother of the Revolution” the ” Iron Woman” and ” the Icon of Arab Spring” Karman played a central role in Yemen’s peaceful uprising, helping mobilize nationwide protests that led to the end of decades-long authoritarian rule in Yemen.

She founded Women Journalists Without Chains in 2005 and the Peaceful Revolutionary Youth Council, both of which played key roles in defending press freedom and advancing democratic change.

She was recently awarded the Guardians of Democracy Prize by the Global Forum for Democracy. TIME named her among the “100 most influential women defining the last century” and described her as the “Torchbearer of the Arab Spring.” and listed her as one of the “Most Rebellious Women in History.”. She has also been recognized among Foreign Policy’s Top Global Thinkers.

Karman served on the United Nations Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel of Eminent Persons on the Post-2015, and currently serves on several international boards, including the Facebook and Instgram Oversight Board. Through the Tawakkol Karman Foundation, she leads major initiatives in education, development, and peacebuilding.

She continues her global struggle against tyranny and corruption and remains a leading advocate for democracy, human rights, and development.
Tena Prelec: Assistant Professor in Politics and International Relations, University of Rijeka
Thabo Limema: Co-Founder, AWACN Men; Chairperson, Absa Men's Forum
Thomas Assam:
Thomas Assam is a Senior Consultant in Governance, Risk & Compliance at Deloitte Austria, where he works with companies and international organizations on building and testing anti-corruption compliance programmes. He also runs anti-corruption workshops and training for multinational companies and international organizations.

Working across Austrian, EU and non-European jurisdictions, he sees up close what happens when the EU framework, the US FCPA and the UK Bribery Act must be reconciled inside a single programme. He examined in his master thesis how companies translate diverging requirements into practice, and where EU rules increasingly set the benchmark beyond Europe's borders. He brings that practitioner's view to the session, which he coordinates and moderates. He is a Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) and holds a master’s degree in international management from the University for Continuing Education Krems and in Global Studies from the University of Vienna.

Zakhona Mvelase: Ms Zakhona Mvelase is the Founder of AWACN, a movement advancing dignity-centred approaches to addressing gendered corruption in Africa.
Zoe Reiter: Anti-kleptocracy director at NED. Co-founder of ACDC. 15+ years partnering globally to dismantle illicit financial flows and authoritarianism.
Zoe Seitz: Zoe Seitz is a Consultant and Senior Expert working at the intersection of business and human rights, sustainable finance, and the regulatory frameworks that shape corporate behaviour. Drawing on a background in strategy consulting and international policy, she examines how tightening EU and global standards reshape business conduct across borders and supply chains. She holds degrees in Business and Economics from WU Vienna and in Human Rights and Diplomacy from the University of Stirling. Bringing a cross-regional, systems-level perspective to questions of corporate accountability and compliance, she speaks regularly at institutions and forums such as the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the University of St. Gallen.
